New profiles use the download settings in Options…. Existing queue items keep their own settings.
Copying a whole following list

Profile → view all next to Following accounts → scroll that list all the way to the bottom until it stops loading, then select all and copy. Copying before it finishes scrolling only picks up the rows that happened to be on screen.

Saved videos

Reads the export TikTok makes for you (Settings → Account → Download your data, JSON) and downloads every saved video into its creator's own folder, making that profile if it is not there yet. Anything already grabbed is skipped — the app keeps its own list of what it has taken, so exporting again only fetches what is new. Everything it takes is filed under the bookmark category TikTok Favorites, so the whole lot is viewable in one place.

TikTok logins are kept in Sessions — every saved login is listed there, with the one downloads use, and each can be renamed or deleted.
Options for this one
Download settings
Files and folders where new downloads are written, and which folders the gallery reads
Downloads are saved into the downloads folder. When that drive reaches the space limit, a new download is written into one of the archive folders below that still has room — one profile always stays on one drive. The gallery shows everything in every folder listed, so old archives can stay on other drives and still appear. Nothing is ever moved without you asking.
Downloads folder new files go here
…
Archive folders everything the gallery shows
The downloads folder is always one of them. A folder marked takes overflow is also where new downloads go once the downloads drive is full, so a second drive keeps the queue moving instead of stopping it. A folder on an unplugged drive simply disappears from the gallery until it is plugged back in.
No settings match that filter.
Excluded profiles people you deleted — nothing downloads them again until you undo it
Excluded profiles
Deleting a profile adds them here, so a pasted list or the automatic check cannot download them again by accident. Undo only clears that memory — their files went to the system Trash, and getting those back is the Trash bin's job.

This app whether the downloader runs by itself when you log in
Start on login run the queue by itself when you log in
When on, the downloader starts at login and picks the queue back up where it left off. Turn it off if you would rather start it yourself.
Backup & restore
Your files are in the archive folders — point a new copy of the app at them and the gallery and shorts rebuild themselves. What cannot rebuild is the app's memory: the queue, download settings, hidden items, bookmarks and the list of people you imported. That is what this zip holds. One automatic backup is kept per day; the newest 7 stay.

Excluded — removed from the queue or deleted; restorable

Pasting a profile or a following list again will not add these back. Nothing is deleted — Restore returns them to the queue.

—
Duplicates — same bytes, two folders
A joint post on Instagram is served from every collaborator's profile, so the same carousel is downloaded into two folders. This compares files by content — size first, then a checksum — within one platform (the same picture on Instagram and TikTok is not a duplicate) and lists the identical ones. Scanning only reads files. Moving is what you press, and it puts copies in that profile's Trash section, where the gallery's Restore brings them back.
